headline: A Reiki master wrote a UK number two, and it's both AI and human
deck: Movin' To The Sun started as an AI demo by a Reiki master, then a DJ and a house legend finished it. The Grammys split it in two. Here is who did which bit, and why that's the question to ask at work.
video_title: AI music or human music? This UK number two is both
comment_question: WHAT LANDED ON YOUR DESK THIS WEEK THAT WAS PART AI, PART HUMAN?

figures.after: We couldn't confirm which of the two made this song's first version.
figures.alt: Suno's custom mode: a box for your lyrics, a box for the style of music, and it turns them into a song with vocals. Screenshot from Tom's Guide.
Deezer, two reports three months apart: AI-made tracks are over 50% of the new music uploaded every day (July 2026) but get 1% to 3% of the listening (April 2026).

figures.after: could still be eligible in the performance categories.
figures.alt: One recording, two answers: out of the Grammys' songwriting categories, could still qualify in performance.

figures.after: with a trace of the AI voice still underneath.
figures.alt: Who did which bit, bottom up: Imael Angel wrote the words; an AI app made the first version with an AI singer; HUGEL rebuilt the track from ready-made parts; Ultra Nate sang it, with a thin AI layer kept under her voice.

figures.after: so the name on a piece of work belongs to the person who stands behind it.
figures.alt: Ask who did which bit: whose idea was it, what did a tool draft, who checked it and put their name to it.
